vocabulary.meaning: A shadow that looks scary and behaves in an unpredictable way.
A very pleasant and sweet smell that comes from magic.
To make the beast very curious and interested.
A very rich, beautiful, and fancy light.
To count his steps in a very exact and careful way.
To be mean by using words that seem nice but are meant to mock or hurt someone.
To wake up his energy and make him feel lively and strong.
To scold or tell off the beast for its bad behavior.
To collapse and break into small pieces, like a piece of paper you squeeze.
To learn a lesson or gain knowledge from something that happened.
To struggle and move clumsily because of a lot of confusion and trouble.
A long and steady look at something.

story:
With the Dragon Egg clutched safely in his arms, Alistair rushed back to his village. He was so tired he could barely keep his eyes open, but the egg’s magic seemed to arouse his spirit (wake up and fill him with energy). He kept a precise count of his steps (an exact and careful count) so he would not get lost in the forest. As he got closer, he saw a swirling cloud of darkness over his village, a menacing and erratic shadow (a scary and unpredictable shadow) that was causing chaos.
The shadow beast was attacking the village, its dark magic making buildings crumple and fall apart (to collapse and break into pieces). The villagers were in a state of tumultuous despair (a lot of sadness and hopelessness), and Alistair could see them flounder in the chaos (struggle and move clumsily). He felt a sudden anger and couldn't help but chide the beast (scold or tell off the beast) for its cruelty.
He ran to the center of the village and gently placed the Dragon Egg on the ground. The egg began to glow, and a beautiful, lavish light (very fancy and rich light) filled the air. A fragrant scent of magic (a pleasant and sweet smell) spread through the village. The light grew stronger, and from the egg emerged a tiny, magnificent dragon!
The dragon gave the shadow beast a long, fiery gaze (a long, steady look) that seemed to intrigue the beast (make the beast very curious). Alistair knew he could derive a lesson from this moment (learn a lesson from this experience): The dragon’s light was not meant to fight the shadow, but to show it a different way. The little dragon sang a beautiful song, and the darkness began to fade. The shadow beast, no longer sarcastic and cruel (mocking and mean), simply dissolved into the light.
The villagers cheered. Their hearts, once full of sorrow and dread, were now full of hope. The dragon had saved them, and Alistair had completed his quest. He had learned that even the smallest light can overcome the darkest shadows. The story of Alistair and the little dragon became a tale of bravery and hope, told for generations to come.
